h1: The Real Cost of Recruitment in 2026: The Numbers Behind the 2022 Figure Everyone Still Quotes

persona.name: Executive & Compliance Buyer
persona.lens: A CHRO/CXO building or defending the hiring budget, who needs an authoritative, current cost-per-hire figure and a defensible hard-vs-soft cost breakdown by role and volume to make the business case internally.
persona.why: Cost-per-hire is business-case/ROI content — the doc routes ROI and total-cost-of-hiring topics to the Executive & Compliance Buyer, the reader who owns and defends that budget number, not the recruiter who just tracks it operationally.

ai_overview: defines cost per hire (CPH) as the average spend to recruit a new employee ($4,500-$4,800 typical range), gives the formula (Internal Costs + External Costs / Total Hires), then groups costs into Internal Costs (prorated recruiter/HR salaries, referral awards, hiring-manager interview time) and External Costs (job board fees, agency/search firm fees, ATS costs, background checks, travel/relocation), notes variance by company size/industry/role seniority (specialized technical or C-suite roles: $15,000-$30,000+), and closes on tracking quarterly against the SHRM Cost-Per-Hire Standard
